claims.text: The starting HfNbTaTiZr-based protective coating has a mixed FCC/BCC structure.
The starting coating exhibits a conventional BCC response and typical creep strain rates during continuous high-temperature loading.
Selecting or adding suitable elements can reduce the critical resolved shear stress for non-traditional slip systems in the BCC phase.
In situ TEM and diffraction can distinguish non-Schmid slip effects from nano-twinning effects.
Fixed-load creep testing at 700–900 °C can activate both traditional Schmid and non-Schmid slip modes in this coating.
The proposed compositional modification alters BCC dislocation-core structures.
The altered dislocation-core structures favor activation of non-Schmid slip modes.
The altered core structures minimize the tendency to form localized shear bands.
Enhanced non-Schmid slip distributes dislocation motion more homogeneously.
More homogeneous dislocation motion suppresses dislocation climb.
More homogeneous dislocation motion suppresses localized shear.
Suppression of dislocation climb and localized shear reduces creep-strain accumulation under sustained loading.
The modified coating will exhibit less localized strain accumulation than the unaltered coating.
The modified coating will exhibit a lower creep strain rate than the unaltered coating.
Greater non-Schmid slip activation will correlate with improved creep resistance.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate at 700–900 °C under fixed loads that stimulate both Schmid and non-Schmid slip systems.
The theoretical basis for improving creep resistance through enhanced non-Schmid slip is strong.
Nano-twinning or other competing mechanisms may contribute to the observed creep response.
